title: Multi-Resonance Mesh-Based Wavelength-Routed Optical Networks-on-Chip
problem: Wavelength-routed optical networks-on-chip (WRONoCs) struggle to simultaneously reduce design complexity and optical power consumption. Each microring resonator (MRR) currently demultiplexes to only one wavelength, significantly increasing MRR usage and insertion loss.
motivation: WRONoCs enable high-speed, collision-free communication in multi-core processors, but reducing power consumption and MRR overhead is critical for practical deployment.
method: The approach adapts different ONoC router types to mesh-based templates and exploits multi-resonance properties of microring resonators, enabling a single MRR to demultiplex signals on multiple wavelengths. An efficient synthesis method combines multi-resonance MRRs with existing optical routers to minimize total power consumption and MRR usage.
key_novelty: Using multi-resonance microring resonators to allow a single resonator to demultiplex multiple wavelengths, reducing both MRR count and insertion loss.
contributions: Exploits multi-resonance capability of MRRs for multi-wavelength demultiplexing
Efficient design methodology for mesh-based WRONoCs using multi-resonance MRRs
Significant reduction in MRR usage and optical power consumption
Adaptation of various optical router types to mesh-based topologies

metrics.other: MRR usage reduction, optical power consumption reduction
